Render a result in gdalraster's in-memory raster format

Source: R/raster.R
xr_raster.Rd

An alternate rendering: where DBI::dbFetch() gives the tidy long-form data frame, xr_raster() gives the slab in the same in-memory form as gdalraster read_ds() a plain vector of pixel values in left-to-right, top-to-bottom order, band-sequential, with a gis attribute carrying type, bbox, dim, srs, and datatype. No dataset is created and no bytes go through GDAL; the array converts directly via numpy (no pandas hop), and gdalraster is not needed at all.

Usage

xr_raster(
  x,
  statement = NULL,
  as_list = FALSE,
  max_cells = getOption("xrdbi.max_cells", 1e+07),
  force = FALSE,
  params = NULL
)

Arguments

x

an XarrayResult, or an XarrayConnection (with statement)

statement

a Python expression, when x is a connection

as_list

if TRUE, a list of band vectors instead of one band-sequential vector

max_cells

guard threshold, as elsewhere

force

bypass the guard

params

named list of values the statement refers to, when x is a connection (see XarrayResult)

Value

a vector (or list of band vectors) with attribute gis, interchangeable with the output of gdalraster read_ds

Details

The selected object must be a DataArray that squeezes to 2 or 3 dimensions: (y, x) for a single band, (band, y, x) for a stack (e.g. a time series of slabs). y and x are taken by position, the last two dimensions, whatever their names: an array stored (lon, lat) renders transposed, so put it in order in the statement (.transpose('lat', 'lon')). The y and x coordinates must be 1-D, numeric and regular (to their storage precision: float32 grids are fine); the half-cell bbox expansion assumes cell-centre coordinates. Ascending or descending coordinate order is handled on either axis (rows and columns are reordered into top-left pixel order). Curvilinear grids have no affine rendering, and vector data cubes (an xvec geometry dimension) no raster at all; both error with the reason.

srs is the CRS found in this order: an index carrying one (xproj's CRSIndex, as gdalxarray sets; rasterix's RasterIndex); WKT in a crs_wkt or spatial_ref attribute of a spatial_ref/crs coordinate, of the variable named by the CF grid_mapping attribute, or of a dataset variable named spatial_ref or crs; and last the CF parameters of that grid_mapping variable, through pyproj when it is installed. "" when none is found.

See also

xr_chunks() for the storage chunks under a slab; XarrayResult for statements and params; xrdbi-package for an overview.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## needs a Python environment with xarray (see ?xrdbi)
f <- system.file("extdata/autotest/trmm.nc", package = "xrdbi")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), f)
r <- xr_raster(con, "ds.pcp.isel(time=0)")
attr(r, "gis")$dim
attr(r, "gis")$bbox

## or from a result
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "ds.pcp.isel(time=0)")
r <- xr_raster(res)
dbClearResult(res)
} # }
